rationale: This is the archive's "Liquidity-Stressed Acquisition Spend" with the identical distress composite and only a 3-year TS_MAX smoothing applied to the same acquisition-intensity leg, a cosmetic persistence tweak rather than a substantively different mechanism.
Expression is literally the archived "Cash-Flow-Strained Capex Acceleration" with RANK swapped for IND_RANK plus a winsorization, i.e., a pure normalization variant with no new economic content.

It recombines two archived components but replaces the generic liquidity composite with a genuinely different conditioning state — an internal capex-versus-operating-cash funding gap — and the sign logic is internally consistent, though it sits in an already heavily mined asset-renewal family.

The two legs are mechanically entangled — high invt/act shrinks the (act - invt) denominator of the second term — so the product largely amplifies inventory concentration rather than testing a true interaction, and it overlaps directly with the archived "Inventory Liquidity Trap"/"Continuous Inventory Liquidity Squeeze".

Conditioning capex acceleration on short-term debt share of total liabilities is a distinct rollover-risk channel not yet tested (archive used lct/act, oancf, or dlc/at with inventory), and the expected negative sign follows naturally from the expression.

This differs from the archived "Non-Goodwill Intangible Loss Build" only by adding IND_RANK and swapping one highly correlated unprofitability proxy set (oancf/re) for another (ni/liquidity), which is a cosmetic variant of an already weak signal.
